newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR says its staff attacked in Zaire, casualties.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR says its staff attacked in Zaire, casualties.

text.p: Local staff members of the U.N. refugee agency have been ambushed in the anarchic eastern Zairean town of Bukavu and there are casualties, a senior U.N. official said on Thursday, quoting unconfirmed reports.

Augustine Mahiga, UNHCR coordinator for Africa's troubled Great Lakes region, told Reuters in Geneva the employees were attacked while they were trying to flee the lakeside town where there is no longer a Western relief presence due to insecurity.

"We have unconfirmed reports that some of our local staff from Bukavu who were trying to leave the town ran into an ambush. We've heard of casualties -- dead and wounded -- but we don't know the numbers, we don't know the location," he said.
He said UNHCR had no details of the attack.
"The situation is getting very messy," he said.

"The most urgent step needed is to secure a ceasefire. And this is beyond the initiatives of humanitarian agencies. It has to come from the United Nations, from countries in the region and from the whole international community."
In the town of Goma further north, Mahiga said UNHCR would evacuate staff members following an outbreak of fighting there between Zairean troops and ethnic Tutsi fighters.
"There are reports the fighting is getting closer to Goma town. Our staff are all indoors, either in hotels or in offices. We're making plans to evacuate them," he said.
He said the evacuation would be by land acroos the nearby Rwandan border to the town of Gisenyi. There are 14 UNHCR expatriate staff members in Goma and another 90 with Western aid agencies.

UNHCR is coordinating agency for Goma and is also responsible for security there. If it pulls out, other agencies are certain to follow, leaving more than 700,000 Rwandan Hutus in the region to their fate.

The Hutus fled in fear of reprisal for 1994's Hutu-led genocide of half a million Tutsis and Hutu moderates. Militia among them used refugee camps on Rwanda's borders as staging posts for attacks into Rwanda. Repeated Rwandan government calls to move the camps away from the borders fell on deaf ears.

If fighting spreads, the refugees in Goma would have two escape routes -- Rwanda where many fear revenge for the genocice, or Masisi region near Goma which is another ethnic warzone where native Zairean tribes are battling local Hutus.

U.N. and other aid agencies have had vehicles stolen and offices looted by drunken Zairean soldiers, and Mahiga said it was impossible for relief agencies to continue work in the absence of a ceasefire.
"We've already pulled out of Bukavu, we've already pulled out of Bukavu. Now if we pull out of Goma, it'll mean no international presence at all," Mahiga said.
"Security is the major constraint. We cannot imagine what will happen to the refugees if there is no assistance. It is really going to be a disaster, a humanitarian catastrophe," he said.
Some 115,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees fled the camp of Kahindo on a mountain valley in the shadow of volcanoes overnight and are heading for Goma town, Mahiga added.

Another 400,000 refugees are crammed into Mugunga camp near Goma town and there are fears that fighting may displace the population of another camp in the region, Katale, home to more than 200,000 Hutus.
Elsewhere more than 400,000 refugees are on the run, fleeing fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels.
